title: First halting time
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x,y$ be binary strings, and let $T\in\mathbb{N}$. If $M$ computes $y$ from $x$ within $T$ steps, then there is a time $t\le T$ such that $M$ has not halted at any time $r<t$, is halted at time $t$, and has output $y$ at time $t$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet
replaced:
Let a finite multi-tape machine $M$ compute output $y$ on input $x$ within $T$
steps. Then there is a time $t \le T$ such that $M$ is still live at every time
before $t$, halts exactly at time $t$, and its output at time $t$ is $y$: the first
halting transition can be selected while retaining the final emission.
